title: Drishyam 3 Arrives May 21 With ₹25 Crore in Pre-Sales — Here's When NRIs Can Stream It
excerpt: Mohanlal's birthday gift to fans may be the biggest Malayalam opening ever, but a legal dispute clouds the Amazon Prime Video streaming timeline
body:
Georgekutty is back — and this time, all of Mollywood is holding its breath.

Mohanlal's **Drishyam 3**, the final chapter of the franchise that redefined Malayalam thriller cinema, hits theatres worldwide on **May 21, 2026** — a date that also happens to be the superstar's 66th birthday. It's the kind of poetic symmetry that Jeethu Joseph, the director who crafted every twist in this saga, would appreciate.

## The Numbers Tell a Story

The advance booking frenzy has been nothing short of extraordinary. Global pre-sales have crossed **₹25 crore**, making it one of the biggest pre-sale performances in Malayalam cinema history. Only *L2: Empuraan* has managed higher opening-day pre-sales in the language, and analysts predict the final figure could push past ₹30 crore before the first show rolls.

The film is releasing simultaneously in **Malayalam, Telugu, and Kannada**, with PEN Studios reportedly investing a staggering **₹100 crore** in the franchise's finale. Produced by Antony Perumbavoor under Aashirvad Cinemas, the project features music by Anil Johnson and cinematography by Satheesh Kurup.

## What We Know About the Plot

Plot details remain tightly guarded, but the broad contours are clear: Georgekutty's carefully constructed world of lies is crumbling. The psychological burden of what he did to protect his family — the central premise that gripped millions across two films — reaches its breaking point. Meena returns alongside Mohanlal, and the film promises to explore whether a man who built his entire life on deception can ever find redemption, or if the truth will consume everything he fought to preserve.

Principal photography wrapped between September and December 2025, with Jeethu Joseph reportedly spending months in post-production perfecting the thriller's pacing.

## The OTT Question Every NRI Is Asking

For the millions of Malayali diaspora viewers scattered across the US, UK, Canada, and the Gulf, one question dominates every WhatsApp family group: *when can we stream it?*

The answer is complicated. Amazon Prime Video holds the streaming rights to the franchise — both previous installments are already on the platform. Reports indicate a **30-to-35-day theatrical window** will be observed, which would place the OTT premiere around **late June or early July 2026**.

But there's a wrinkle. A legal dispute between Amazon Prime Video and Aashirvad Cinemas has cast a shadow over the digital deal. The **Delhi High Court** recently granted interim relief that effectively paused OTT negotiations, and until that matter resolves, the streaming timeline remains uncertain. For NRIs planning watch parties, the safest bet is to catch it in theatres if your city has a screening — and most major metros in the US and UK will.

## Why This Matters for Diaspora Audiences

The original *Drishyam* (2013) wasn't just a Malayalam hit — it became a cultural phenomenon that spawned remakes in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and Kannada. The Hindi version starring Ajay Devgn introduced millions of non-Malayali viewers to the story. *Drishyam 2* (2021) was one of Amazon Prime Video's most-watched Indian films globally during the pandemic, with NRI viewership driving a significant portion of its numbers.

This finale carries the weight of a decade-long narrative that has genuinely crossed linguistic and geographic barriers — a rare feat in Indian cinema.

## What's Next

All eyes are on the May 21 opening. If the pre-sales trajectory holds, Drishyam 3 could challenge *L2: Empuraan* for the biggest Malayalam opening ever. For Mohanlal, it's a chance to cap his most iconic role with a birthday release that fans have been dreaming about for years.

For NRIs: check BookMyShow International and local listings for screenings near you. And if you're waiting for the couch-and-biryani OTT premiere — patience. It's coming. The legal clouds will clear, and Georgekutty's final confession will find its way to your screen.
